name: Clindamycin Hydrochloride
sections: White crystalline powder (hydrochloride), freely soluble in water.

On the WHO List of Essential Medicines; important for anaerobic, bone and MRSA skin infections and toxin suppression in necrotising infections. First approval/introduction: Synthesised 1966 from lincomycin; approved 1968 (The Upjohn Company).

Binds the 50S ribosomal subunit, inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis (bacteriostatic; bactericidal at higher concentrations). Active against Gram-positive cocci (including many MRSA) and anaerobes; inhibits toxin production. Receptor / target profile: Binds 23S rRNA of the 50S ribosomal subunit inhibiting protein synthesis; bacteriostatic (bactericidal at high concentrations); suppresses toxin production.

Summary: Bioavailability ~90%; Tmax ~45 min. ~94% protein bound. Excellent bone and tissue penetration. Hepatic metabolism (CYP3A4). Half-life ~2.4 h.
